- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend; prioritize sentiment direction over historical mean.
